subject: Materials Science
title: Precipitate Interfaces
description: A quick, practical guide to Precipitate Interfaces.

hook.text: Age an aluminum alloy at 170°C and tiny particles form inside — the metal gets twice as strong.

buildup.text: Precipitates are small particles of a different phase that nucleate and grow within the matrix.

discovery.text: The interface between precipitate and matrix can be coherent, semi-coherent, or incoherent.

twist.text: Coherent precipitates strain the lattice — this strain field is what blocks dislocations most effectively.

climax.text: Aircraft aluminum alloys (2024, 7075) get their strength from precisely controlled precipitate aging.

punchline.text: Tiny particles trapped in a crystal lattice can make metal fly.

quiz.question: Why do coherent precipitates strengthen metals?
options: Their lattice strain blocks dislocation movement
They remove all vacancies from the crystal
